paper.title: Logarithmic Regret for Online KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning

unmapped: Regret measured on the KL-regularized objective J(pi) = E[R*(x,a)] - (1/eta) KL(pi || pi_ref), with known reference policy pi_ref and known regularization parameter eta
Mean reward function R* in [0,1] lies in a known finite class R (realizability)
Learner uses a planning oracle to compute Gibbs policies
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \ge 1$, the learner observes a context $x_t \in \cX$, and chooses an action $a_t \in \cA$ ... $r_t = R^*(x_t, a_t) + \epsilon_t$, where $R^*(x_t, a_t)$ is the unknown reward function and $\epsilon_t$ is an independent 1-sub-Gaussian zero-mean random noise. ... $J(\pi) := \rE_{x \sim d_0} \rE_{a \sim \pi(\cdot | x)} [R^*(x, a) - \frac{1}{\eta} \log \frac{\pi(a|x)}{\pi_{\reff}(a|x)}]$

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic MDP (reinforcement learning) with function approximation
unmapped: KL-regularized value objective with reference policy
Q* realizability and KL-regularized Bellman completeness
bonus function class with finite cardinality
settings.definition_quote: A Markov Decision Process (MDP) is defined by a tuple $\cM = (\cS, \cA, H, \PP, d_0, r)$ ... The objective is to find a policy $\pi$ that maximizes the following KL-regularized value: $J(\pi) = \E^{\pi} [\sum_{h = 1}^H r_h (s_h, a_h) - \eta^{-1} \sum_{h = 1}^H \log \frac{\pi_h(a_h|s_h)}{\pi_{\reff,h}(a_h|s_h)}]$

symbols.N_R: cardinality of the reward function class R
symbols.d_R: eluder dimension d(R, lambda, T) of the reward class (magnitude-weighted variant, Definition 3.3)

conditions: R* belongs to a known finite class R with values in [0,1] (Assumption 3.2)

source.label: th:bandit
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{as:Reward function realizability}, for any $\delta>0$, by taking $\beta_T=16\log(N_{\cR}T/\delta)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:kl-bandits} satisfies $\mathrm{Regret}(T) = \cO\Big(\eta\log(N_{\cR}T/\delta)\cdot d(\cR,\lambda,T)\Big).$

results.notes: Regret is sum_t J(pi*) - J(pi_t) of the KL-regularized objective (expectation over contexts and actions inside J), holding w.p. 1-delta over the data. Comparator is the optimal regularized policy. Not comparable to standard unregularized regret.

symbols.d_F: sum over h of eluder dimensions d(F_h, lambda, T)
symbols.N_FB: max_h N_{F_h} * N_{F_{h+1}} * N_{B_{h+1}} (cardinalities of value and bonus classes)

conditions: bonus functions lie in finite class B_h

source.label: th:mdp
source.quote: Under Algorithm \ref{alg:kl-mdp} and Assumptions \ref{as:Realizability} and \ref{as:Bellman completeness} with $\beta_h^T = \Theta(\sqrt{\log(N_h T H / \delta)})$, we have with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\mathrm{Regret}(T) = \cO\Big(\eta H^2 d(\cF,\lambda,T) \cdot \log(N_{\cF\oplus\cB} TH /\delta)\Big)$

results.notes: Episodic RL setting (out of scope). T is number of episodes. Regret on KL-regularized value.
